certificate.title: Financial Modeling with Claude as a CFO Completion

course.description: *Adapted from Wouter Born — [linkedin.com/in/wouterborn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/wouterborn)* A step-by-step workflow for finance leaders to go from planning model to board-ready dashboard in 20 minutes using Claude. Replace your 3-5 day monthly FP&A cycle with a repeatable AI-powered process. ---
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Financial Modeling with Claude as a CFO.

modules.description: Create a persistent, reusable workspace that gets smarter every month.

lessons.content:
In Claude, create a new Project — think of it as a dedicated CFO workspace that holds memory across every session. Unlike a regular chat, your Project retains context, instructions, and uploaded files month over month.

Name it something like **"Monthly FP&A — [Company Name]"** so it's easy to return to each cycle.
lessons.title: Create Your Claude Project

lessons.content:
Before uploading anything, write your standing instructions directly into the Project. This is your CFO brief to Claude. Include:

- Your company's fiscal calendar and reporting periods
- How your model is structured (revenue lines, cost centers, etc.)
- Your preferred terminology (e.g., "reforecast" vs "rolling forecast")
- Output preferences (e.g., "always show variance to prior plan")
- Tone for board narratives (e.g., "concise, no jargon, lead with insight")

These instructions persist and are applied automatically every time you work in this Project.

---
lessons.title: Define Your Project Instructions

modules.title: Set Up Your Claude Project

modules.description: Give Claude everything it needs to understand your numbers in context.

lessons.content:
Structure your workbook with four sheets before uploading:

| Sheet | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **Sales** | Revenue actuals and forecast by period |
| **HQ** | Headcount, overhead, corporate costs |
| **Financials** | P&L, cash, key metrics |
| **Instructions** | Model logic, definitions, named ranges |

The Instructions sheet is critical — it tells Claude how your model works so it doesn't have to guess at formulas or logic.
lessons.title: Upload Your Four Core Sheets

lessons.content: Export your actuals directly from your ERP system (NetSuite, SAP, Dynamics, etc.) and upload alongside the workbook. This gives Claude a clean, authoritative source of truth for the period.
lessons.title: Upload Your ERP Export

lessons.content:
Claude weighs inputs in this order when there is conflicting information:

1. **ERP exports** — highest trust, hard actuals
2. **Your instructions** — your defined logic and preferences
3. **Prior outputs** — last month's dashboard for continuity
4. **Claude's own reasoning** — fills gaps only when needed

Knowing this helps you troubleshoot if outputs ever look unexpected.

---
lessons.title: Understand the Priority Hierarchy

modules.title: Upload Your Source Materials

modules.description: Let Claude inspect, map, and advance your model — in minutes.

lessons.content:
Use a single rollover prompt that does three things at once. Example:

> *"Review the uploaded model and ERP export. Map actuals vs forecast for the cutoff date. Load April actuals into the model. Move the forecast forward one period and flag any structural issues you find."*

Claude will first inspect the model before touching anything — checking for formula breaks, missing data, or structural changes that could affect accuracy.
lessons.title: Prompt the Rollover

activities.title: Review the Actuals vs Forecast Map

lessons.content:
Claude will produce a comparison showing where actuals landed versus your prior forecast. Review this output before moving forward. Look for:

- Significant variances (positive or negative)
- Lines where ERP data didn't map cleanly to model categories
- Any periods where Claude flagged low confidence

This is your checkpoint before the reforecast begins.

---
lessons.title: Review the Actuals vs Forecast Map

modules.title: Run the Monthly Rollover

modules.description: Translate real-world decisions into model updates using plain English.

lessons.content:
No need to manually adjust cells. Describe your management changes conversationally. For example:

> *"VP Marketing budget increased to $210K. Account Exec hiring adds $140K. AI tools budget up $120K per month. Professional services cut by $156K. Pipeline ramp adjusted — push Q3 target by 6 weeks."*

Claude reads the changes, applies them to the correct model lines, and maintains an audit trail of every adjustment made.
lessons.title: Input Your Key Changes

lessons.content:
Before finalizing, Claude shows you a side-by-side comparison of:

- **New assumptions** vs **prior plan**
- The financial impact of each change
- Any downstream effects on cash runway or EBITDA

This is your last chance to course-correct before the dashboard is built. Push back on anything that looks wrong — Claude will adjust.

---
lessons.title: Review the Assumption Delta

modules.title: Apply Management Changes

modules.description: Go from updated model to presentation-ready output automatically.

lessons.content:
Prompt Claude to build your dashboard with sensitivity analysis across three scenarios:

> *"Build a board-ready dashboard from the reforecast. Include Base, Downside, and Upside scenarios. Show KPI cards for Revenue, EBITDA, and Cash Runway. Include a sensitivity matrix."*

Claude will produce:

- **KPI Cards** — Revenue, EBITDA, Cash Runway at a glance
- **Scenario toggle** — Base / Downside / Upside views
- **Sensitivity matrix** — showing how key variables affect outcomes
- **Variance commentary** — written narrative explaining the numbers
lessons.title: Generate the Three-Scenario Dashboard

lessons.content:
Claude delivers two outputs:

- **HTML dashboard** — ready to present or share as a link
- **Downloadable Excel** — for your finance team or audit trail

The HTML dashboard is interactive and scenario-aware — far more useful in a board meeting than a static slide deck.

---
lessons.title: Export Your Outputs

modules.title: Build the Board Dashboard

modules.description: Turn numbers into a planning story, not a chart dump.

lessons.content:
Ask Claude to write the board narrative based on everything it now knows:

> *"Write a board-ready narrative summary. Lead with the most important insight. Flag key risks and opportunities. Keep it under 300 words, no jargon."*

Because Claude has full context from the reforecast — including what changed, why, and what the scenarios show — the narrative is grounded and specific, not generic.
lessons.title: Generate the Executive Narrative

lessons.content:
Each month you run this workflow, Claude gets more useful:

- ✅ **Assumptions carry forward** — no re-explaining your model logic
- ✅ **Audit trail grows** — every change is documented and traceable
- ✅ **Narratives improve** — Claude learns your business and board's preferences
- ✅ **Cycle compresses** — what started at 20 minutes gets faster

The goal is a planning copilot that learns your business — not a chatbot doing math.

---

> **Total time: ~20 minutes** | *Replaces a 3-5 day manual FP&A cycle*
